title: The Role of Contrast in Chest CT in Older Patients with Low Energy Injury Mechanisms: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study
content: Background: This single centre retrospective case note review evaluated the injuries sustained in older patients with low energy transfer mechanisms of injury, and established which of these injury types required contrast-enhanced CT for their identification, characterisation or to inform management. Materials and Methods: We identified all patients >65 who underwent CT chest for trauma over a 2-year period. Patients with a high energy transfer mechanism were excluded. Identified injuries were categorised by type, and whether contrast was used during CT. Two radiologists independently suggested which injuries would have benefitted from contrast use for identification or characterisation; they were in full agreement. Cases where these injuries were identified were reviewed to establish: whether contrast was used (either initially or on follow-up); what interventions were required; and whether the patient died during the admission. Results: The review identified 475 cases; 251 were eligible for inclusion. Of these, 220 (87.6%) underwent contrast-enhanced CT thorax as their initial investigation. Seven injury types were identified where contrast may have been useful for identification or characterisation. One or more of these injuries were found in 9 cases (3.6%), only 5 of which underwent contrast-enhanced CT imaging at any point during routine care. None of these patients received any injury-specific interventions. Conclusions: Contrast use appears to add little value to the identification or management of injuries in older patients with low energy transfer mechanisms of injury. Further research should prospectively evaluate the implementation of non-contrast CT protocols in this cohort.
